verses.text: One day Jonathan son of Saul told his young armor-bearer, “Come with me to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” He didn't tell his father.
Saul was on the outskirts of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree at Migron. About six hundred men were with him.
Ahijah, who wore an ephod, was among them. He was the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, the LORD's priest at Shiloh. The troops didn't know Jonathan had left.
There was a steep rock on either side of the pass Jonathan wanted to take to the Philistine outpost. One was called Bozez and the other Seneh.
One stood to the north facing Michmash, and the other stood to the south facing Geba.
Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “Come on. Let's cross to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Maybe the LORD will act for us. Nothing keeps the LORD from saving by many or by few.”
His armor-bearer said, “Do whatever you have in mind. Go ahead. I'm with you all the way.”
Jonathan said, “We'll cross over and let those men see us.
If they tell us, ‘Wait there until we come to you,’ we'll stay where we are and won't go up.
If they say, ‘Come up to us,’ we'll go up, because the LORD has handed them over to us. That will be our sign.”
They showed themselves to the Philistine outpost. The Philistines said, “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they've been hiding!”
The men at the outpost called to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come up here and we'll show you something!” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “Follow me up. The LORD has handed them over to Israel.”
Jonathan scrambled up on his hands and feet with his armor-bearer behind him. Men fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed, killing them.
In that first attack, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men within roughly half a furrow's length in a field.
Panic spread through the camp, the field, the outpost, and the raiding parties. The earth shook, and everyone was terrified.
Saul's lookouts at Gibeah in Benjamin saw the Philistine army dissolve and scatter.
Saul told his men, “Count everyone and find out who's missing.” When they counted, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were gone.
Saul told Ahijah to bring God's ark, because the ark was with the Israelites at that time.
While Saul was speaking to the priest, the uproar in the Philistine camp grew louder. Saul told the priest, “Take your hand away!”
Saul and all his men rushed to the battle and found the Philistines in complete confusion, striking one another with their swords.
The Hebrews who had previously joined the Philistines in their camp switched sides and joined the Israelites with Saul and Jonathan.
When the Israelites who'd been hiding in Ephraim's hill country heard the Philistines were fleeing, they joined the pursuit too.
The LORD rescued Israel that day, and the fighting spread beyond Beth Aven.
The Israelites were in distress that day because Saul had put them under an oath: “Cursed is anyone who eats before evening, before I've taken revenge on my enemies.” So nobody tasted any food.
The whole army came into the woods, where there was honey on the ground.
They saw honey dripping, but no one tasted it because they were afraid of breaking the oath.
Jonathan hadn't heard his father's oath. He dipped the tip of his staff into the honeycomb and tasted the honey, and his eyes brightened.
One of the men told him, “Your father put everyone under a strict oath. He said, ‘Cursed is anyone who eats today.’” The men were exhausted.
Jonathan said, “My father has brought trouble on the land. Look how my eyes brightened after I tasted just a little honey.
How much better would it have been if everyone had eaten freely from what they took from their enemies today? We could have struck down many more Philistines.”
That day they struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon. The troops were worn out.
They rushed to the plunder, took sheep, cattle, and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground. Then they ate the meat with the blood still in it.
Someone told Saul, “The people are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood.” Saul said, “You've broken faith. Roll a large stone over here now.”

He told his men to go through the crowd and say, “Bring your cattle and sheep here. Slaughter them here and eat, so you don't sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood.” That night everyone brought their cattle and slaughtered them there.
Saul built an altar to the LORD. It was the first altar he'd built for him.
Saul said, “Let's pursue the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn. Leave none of them alive.” The men answered, “Do whatever seems right to you.” The priest said, “Let's ask God first.”
Saul asked God, “Should I go after the Philistines? Will you hand them over to Israel?” But God didn't answer him that day.
Saul said, “Come here, all you leaders. Let's find out who's responsible for today's sin.
As surely as the LORD who rescues Israel lives, even if my own son Jonathan is guilty, he will die.” Nobody answered him.
Saul told all Israel, “Stand over on one side. My son Jonathan and I will stand on the other.” The people said, “Do what seems right to you.”
Saul prayed to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Show us who is in the right.” Saul and Jonathan were selected, and the people were cleared.
Saul said, “Cast lots between me and my son Jonathan.” Jonathan was selected.
Saul told Jonathan, “Tell me what you did.” Jonathan answered, “I tasted a little honey from the end of my staff. And now I have to die.”
Saul said, “May God deal with me severely if you don't die, Jonathan.”

The people told Saul, “Should Jonathan die after bringing Israel this great victory? Never! As surely as the LORD lives, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground. He worked with God today.” So the people rescued Jonathan, and he didn't die.
Saul stopped pursuing the Philistines, and they went back to their own land.
After taking the throne of Israel, Saul fought enemies on every side: Moab, Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he defeated them.
He fought bravely and struck down the Amalekites, rescuing Israel from those who had been plundering them.
Saul's sons were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. His older daughter was Merab, and his younger daughter was Michal.
Saul's wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle, commanded his army.
Kish was Saul's father, and Ner, Abner's father, was the son of Abiel.
The fighting against the Philistines was fierce throughout Saul's life. Whenever he saw a strong or brave man, he recruited him into his service.
